hypothesis: For enterprise localization workloads, integrating cleaned translation memories (TM), enforced terminology (glossaries), and vector-based example retrieval into an AI-driven translation pipeline will (a) improve linguistic and terminological quality, (b) increase adherence to style and brand voice, and (c) reduce human post-editing effort and cycle time, compared to an otherwise identical pipeline that does not use these linguistic assets.

baseline.description: AI-driven localization pipeline without explicit use of translation memories, termbases, or vector-retrieved examples. The system relies solely on a general-purpose MT/LLM engine plus minimal generic constraints.
pipeline_steps: Content ingestion from prepared test set (JSON/CSV/XLIFF).
Language detection (for validation only; not used for routing here).
Segment-level translation using a single, fixed MT or LLM engine with default or lightly customized prompt (no TM or glossary injection).
Light structural QA: placeholder/tag preservation, length ratio checks, basic script checks.
Export of translations for offline human post-editing and evaluation.

configuration.mt_engine: Configured MT or LLM provider (e.g., open-source MT model or commercial MT/LLM via API) with a fixed model version and deterministic decoding settings where possible (e.g., temperature=0 for LLMs).
configuration.prompt_template_llm: You are a professional translator. Translate the following text from {source_lang} to {target_lang}, preserving meaning and formatting.

treatment.description: AI-driven localization pipeline that integrates cleaned translation memories, enforced termbases, and vector search over example translations/style snippets, keeping all other components aligned with the baseline.
pipeline_steps: Inventory and cleaning of TMs and termbases (pre-experiment; see required_environment and run_instructions).
Content ingestion from the same prepared test set as baseline.
Language detection and validation of expected language pairs.
Per-segment TM lookup with configurable fuzzy threshold (e.g., 75–85%) and penalty model; use of exact/FUZZY matches where applicable.
Terminology application and enforcement: injecting term pairs and non-translatable lists into MT/LLM calls; post-generation terminology checking and optional constrained re-generation where possible.
Vector search against a sentence-level or paragraph-level embedding index built from curated bilingual corpora and style guides; retrieval of top-k similar examples and style patterns per segment.

Segment-level translation using the same MT/LLM engine as baseline, but with: (a) TM matches provided as candidates, (b) glossary constraints, and (c) retrieved examples and style hints embedded in the prompt or adapter logic.
Post-generation QA: structural checks (as baseline) plus terminology adherence checks and optional automatic correction for straightforward violations.
Export of translations for offline human post-editing and evaluation (same format as baseline).
Logging of TM hits, terminology violations, and vector retrieval metadata for ROI analysis.

tm_sources: Cleaned bilingual TMs for at least two language pairs (e.g., en->fr, en->de) in standard formats such as TMX or aligned CSV/TSV.
termbase_sources: Termbase files (e.g., TBX/CSV) including preferred terms, forbidden terms, part-of-speech, domain, and status.

vector_store.embedding_model: Sentence-level multilingual embedding model (e.g., LaBSE, multilingual-MiniLM, or equivalent) with fixed version.
vector_store.index_type: FAISS or equivalent approximate nearest neighbor index.
corpus: Approved style snippets and microcopy (e.g., UI strings, marketing taglines) tagged with language, market, and domain.

configuration.prompt_template_llm:
You are a professional translator working for a regulated enterprise.
Translate the following source text from {source_lang} to {target_lang}.

Follow these requirements:
- Use the preferred terms from the glossary exactly as given.
- Respect non-translatable items; leave them unchanged.
- Follow the style and tone demonstrated in the examples.
- If a high-quality TM candidate is provided, treat it as the primary suggestion unless it is clearly wrong.

Glossary entries (source -> target):
{glossary_entries}

Non-translatable items:
{non_translatables}

TM candidate translations (if any):
{tm_candidates}

Style examples (source -> target):
{style_examples}

Source text:
{source_text}

workloads.name: workload-marketing-high-style
workloads.description: Marketing and brand copy with strong style and terminology requirements (e.g., homepage hero, product landing pages, email headlines).

content_characteristics.asset_overlap_expectation: High overlap with existing TMs and termbases; strong style guidance available.

workloads.tm_coverage_annotation: Include metadata estimating per-segment TM fuzzy match score for analysis (computed offline).

workloads.name: workload-product-ui-terminology-heavy
workloads.description: Product UI strings and in-app messages with strict terminology and non-translatable requirements (e.g., feature names, legal notices in-app).

content_characteristics.asset_overlap_expectation: Very high termbase coverage; moderate TM coverage.

workloads.tm_coverage_annotation: Per-segment TM fuzziness tags and term coverage flags included in metadata.

workloads.name: workload-support-knowledgebase-mixed
workloads.description: Support/knowledge base articles with mixed style needs but high consistency expectations across versions.

content_characteristics.asset_overlap_expectation: Moderate TM coverage; partial termbase coverage; style guidance weaker than marketing domain.

workloads.tm_coverage_annotation: Metadata with TM fuzziness and domain tags for sub-analysis.

data_controls: Use identical source segments and language pairs for baseline and treatment across all workloads.
Randomize segment processing order but ensure both baseline and treatment see the same order within each run (controlled random seed).
Split data into calibration set (for prompt/treshold tuning) and evaluation set; never tune on evaluation set.
Ensure that reference translations used for evaluation are not directly taken from TMs used in the treatment (avoid trivial leakage); if unavoidable, mark such segments for separate reporting.
model_controls: Use the same MT/LLM model version, decoding parameters, and API region for baseline and treatment.
Fix random seeds where supported (e.g., for open-source models); for APIs without deterministic guarantees, run multiple repetitions and report mean/variance.

Disable vendor-side glossary/TM features in both conditions unless they can be configured identically; the differential factor must remain the explicit TM/termbase/vector logic implemented in this experiment.
environment_controls: Run baseline and treatment in the same compute environment (same container image, hardware, and dependency versions).
Throttle or batch requests identically across conditions to reduce effects of rate limiting and latency spikes.
Log all configuration (YAML/JSON) snapshots with a run_id to ensure reproducibility.
human_evaluation_controls: Use the same pool of professional linguists for both baseline and treatment outputs, blinded to condition.
Randomize presentation order of segments and conditions in the evaluation UI.
Provide consistent, written evaluation guidelines with examples of acceptable/unacceptable terminology and style.
Enforce calibration: evaluators must rate a small shared calibration set and achieve acceptable inter-rater agreement before evaluating the full set.

metrics.name: automatic_bleu
metrics.description: Corpus-level BLEU score comparing system output to reference translations, computed per workload and language pair.

metrics.name: automatic_comet
metrics.unit: COMET score (model-dependent scale, typically -1 to 1 or 0–1)
metrics.description: Reference-based COMET scores for translation quality, computed per segment and aggregated by workload.

metrics.name: terminology_accuracy
metrics.description: Proportion of required glossary occurrences that are correctly realized with preferred target terms and no forbidden terms, computed over segments with at least one glossary term.

metrics.name: terminology_violation_rate
metrics.description: Proportion of segments containing at least one usage of a forbidden term or missing a required term.

metrics.name: style_consistency_score
metrics.description: Average human rating of style/voice consistency with provided style guide and examples, on a 1–5 scale.

metrics.name: overall_human_quality_score
metrics.description: Average human rating of overall translation quality (meaning, fluency, terminology, style) per segment.

metrics.name: post_editing_effort_time
metrics.description: Average time taken by professional linguists to post-edit a segment to approval quality, measured via annotation tool logs.

metrics.name: post_editing_keystrokes
metrics.description: Average number of editing keystrokes (insertions, deletions) performed to finalize a segment.

metrics.name: asset_hit_rate_tm
metrics.description: Proportion of segments in the treatment condition where a TM match above the configured fuzziness threshold was found and used.

metrics.name: asset_hit_rate_termbase
metrics.description: Proportion of segments in the treatment condition that contain at least one term from the termbase.

metrics.name: asset_hit_rate_vector
metrics.description: Proportion of segments in the treatment condition where the vector search returned at least one example above the similarity threshold.

metrics.name: cycle_time_pipeline
metrics.description: End-to-end machine pipeline time from ingestion to export per 1000 source characters for baseline and treatment.

metrics.name: estimated_roi
metrics.unit: currency (e.g., USD) per month at scale
metrics.description: Derived metric combining post-editing effort reduction and asset maintenance cost to estimate net monthly savings given assumed volume; formula documented in evidence schema.

primary: Terminology accuracy improves by at least 15 percentage points (absolute) in the treatment vs baseline, with p < 0.05 on a segment-level statistical test (e.g., McNemar's test on matched segments).
Average post_editing_effort_time decreases by at least 20% in the treatment vs baseline for at least two of the three workloads, with p < 0.05 (paired test on segment-level times).
secondary: Overall_human_quality_score increases by at least 0.3 points on the 1–5 scale in the treatment vs baseline for at least two workloads.
Style_consistency_score increases by at least 0.3 points on the 1–5 scale in the marketing workload.
Estimated_roi is positive under realistic volume and rate assumptions documented in the experiment configuration.
Automatic_comet improves significantly (e.g., effect size d >= 0.3) on segments with TM or termbase hits, while not degrading materially (no drop greater than 0.1) on segments without assets.
interpretation_notes: If treatment improves terminology accuracy and post-edit effort but slightly increases cycle_time_pipeline, this can still be considered successful if ROI remains positive under documented assumptions.
Results should be stratified by TM coverage tiers (e.g., no match, low fuzzy, high fuzzy) and termbase presence to understand where assets contribute the most.

failure_modes.name: overfitting_to_tm_errors
failure_modes.description: Treatment may propagate incorrect or outdated TM entries more consistently, harming quality despite higher asset usage metrics.
failure_modes.detection: Manual review of a sample of segments where treatment quality is rated lower than baseline and where a TM hit was used.
failure_modes.mitigation: Flag TM segments with repeated low human scores for cleanup; re-run experiment with cleaned TM subset.

failure_modes.name: terminology_over_constraining
failure_modes.description: Strict glossary enforcement may produce unnatural or grammatically incorrect sentences, especially in languages with complex morphology.
failure_modes.detection: Compare human fluency ratings and error annotations focusing on morphology/grammar issues in segments with multiple enforced terms.
failure_modes.mitigation: Switch from hard to soft glossary enforcement for specific languages; allow inflected variants; enhance prompt with examples of correct inflection.

failure_modes.name: vector_retrieval_noise
failure_modes.description: Poorly tuned vector search may retrieve off-domain or mismatched style examples that confuse the MT/LLM.
failure_modes.detection: Analyze segments with decreased human quality in treatment and high similarity scores from vector search.
failure_modes.mitigation: Tighten similarity threshold, filter examples by domain/market tags, or limit the number of examples included.

failure_modes.name: evaluation_bias_from_tm_references
failure_modes.description: If reference translations are identical or highly similar to TMs used in treatment, it may inflate quality metrics.
failure_modes.detection: Compute similarity between references and TM entries; mark affected segments and analyze separately.
failure_modes.mitigation: Exclude segments with high TM–reference overlap from primary metric calculations; report them as a separate stratum.

failure_modes.name: tooling_latency_and_cost_spikes
failure_modes.description: Additional TM lookups and vector searches may significantly increase latency or compute cost, reducing practical value.
failure_modes.detection: Monitor cycle_time_pipeline and per-segment cost estimates; compare baseline vs treatment.
failure_modes.mitigation: Cache TM/vector results, reduce top_k, or scope assets only to high-risk content types.

failure_modes.name: asset_governance_violations
failure_modes.description: Ingesting or indexing sensitive TMs without proper access controls may violate data governance policies.
failure_modes.detection: Pre-run audit of TM/termbase sources; verification that PII and confidential data are handled per policy.
failure_modes.mitigation: Redact or anonymize sensitive data prior to indexing; enforce access controls and encryption in storage.

runtime.notebooks: Jupyter or equivalent for exploratory analysis and plots.

evaluation_and_annotation: streamlit or a lightweight web framework for human evaluation UI
sqlite3 or simple database for logging human ratings and post-editing actions

mt_or_llm_provider.description: Either an on-prem open-source MT/LLM served via HTTP or a commercial MT/LLM API.
requirements: Stable model version across the entire experiment.
Ability to fix decoding parameters (e.g., temperature, max_tokens).
Documented data handling to satisfy enterprise governance (no training on customer data unless explicitly allowed).

storage.tm_and_termbase_storage: Secure file storage or database; read-only for experiment runs.
storage.vector_index_storage: Local disk or managed volume mounted into the container.

translation_memories: TMX or CSV/TSV files for each workload language pair, stored under repository/data/ch11/tm/.
Prior to experiment, run a cleaning script to remove duplicates, misaligned segments, and marked-invalid entries.
termbases: TBX or CSV files with columns: source_term, target_term, language_pair, domain, status, forbidden_flag.
style_guides_and_examples: Short style guides in markdown or PDF for each domain-language pair.
Curated parallel examples with style tags under repository/data/ch11/style_examples/.

access_control: Restrict raw TM and termbase directories to authorized users.
Enforce read-only mounts for TM/termbase paths in runtime containers.
logging: Do not log full raw source or target content in plaintext in shared logs; instead, log hashed identifiers and aggregate metrics.
Separate audit logs (with content) stored in a restricted-access area for reproducibility and compliance.

preparation: Build the Docker image (recommended): docker build -t ailoc-ch11:latest -f ../envs/ch11/Dockerfile .
Prepare a configuration file: cp configs/ch11_default.yaml configs/ch11_experiment.yaml and adjust paths and provider keys as necessary.

Run TM and termbase cleaning scripts: python scripts/clean_tm.py --config configs/ch11_experiment.yaml and python scripts/clean_termbase.py --config configs/ch11_experiment.yaml; outputs go to data/ch11/cleaned_tm and data/ch11/cleaned_termbase.
Build the vector index: python scripts/build_vector_index.py --config configs/ch11_experiment.yaml; store index in data/ch11/vector_index/.
execution_steps:
Run baseline pipeline on all workloads:
  docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/app ailoc-ch11:latest \
    python pipelines/run_pipeline.py \
      --config configs/ch11_experiment.yaml \
      --mode baseline \
      --workloads workload-marketing-high-style workload-product-ui-terminology-heavy workload-support-knowledgebase-mixed \
      --run_id baseline_v1

Run treatment pipeline on all workloads:
  docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/app ailoc-ch11:latest \
    python pipelines/run_pipeline.py \
      --config configs/ch11_experiment.yaml \
      --mode treatment \
      --workloads workload-marketing-high-style workload-product-ui-terminology-heavy workload-support-knowledgebase-mixed \
      --run_id treatment_v1
Verify that outputs for baseline and treatment are stored in distinct directories (e.g., outputs/baseline_v1/ and outputs/treatment_v1/) with aligned segment IDs.

Launch human evaluation UI (if enabled in config) to collect human ratings and post-editing signals; evaluators should see randomized, blinded pairs of outputs:
  docker run --rm -p 8501:8501 -v $(pwd):/app ailoc-ch11:latest \
    streamlit run eval/human_eval_app.py -- \
      --config configs/ch11_experiment.yaml \
      --runs baseline_v1 treatment_v1
Collect enough human evaluations to meet the sample size specified in configs/ch11_experiment.yaml (e.g., at least 200 rated segments per condition per workload).

Run analysis script to compute metrics and generate comparison tables/plots:
  docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/app ailoc-ch11:latest \
    python analysis/compare_assets_vs_no_assets.py \
      --config configs/ch11_experiment.yaml \
      --baseline_run baseline_v1 \
      --treatment_run treatment_v1 \
      --output_dir analysis/results_ch11_exp1
post_run: Review analysis artifacts: metrics_summary.json, per_segment_metrics.csv, and plots under analysis/results_ch11_exp1/.
Document any deviations from the default configuration (e.g., alternative embedding model, different TM thresholds) in a run_notes.md file stored alongside results.
If repeating the experiment (e.g., with updated TM cleaning or different thresholds), increment run_id (e.g., baseline_v2, treatment_v2) and preserve prior results for comparison.

fields.timestamp_utc: ISO 8601 timestamp when analysis was executed
fields.git_commit_hash: string, commit hash of repository at run time
fields.config_path: string path to the YAML config used
fields.notes: free-text field for deviations or special conditions
